cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Thank you for apologising for missing my concert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Closer. Now why did I have to ask whether you'd noticed missing it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know what to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for letting me rehearse your apology alone all week.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 acknowledges apology; A3 judges B closure request as only closer and demands an account; A5 directs apology for silence rather than merely missed attendance.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 okay question to deny full closure; A5 uses B4 speechlessness to name the burden of imagining the apology alone.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks reconciliation and B4 admits uncertainty, a plausible explanation rather than convenient obstruction.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 failure to find words into a second injury, developing the concert absence rather than adding an unrelated grievance.

specificity.evidence: A1 missed concert apology and A5 week of silence supply understandable personal stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 rehearsing apology is figurative but concrete enough after concert context; prefixes remain redundant.
